profile.headline: Engineering Lead at FORM × Trax | Building high-performing teams and resilient, scalable platforms
profile.summary:
I lead engineering teams that own hard systems with confidence.

Most of my time goes to the parts of engineering that happen outside the editor: growing engineers, scoping and resourcing work, and keeping the team aligned with product, customer-facing teams, and leadership. I make sure the value we deliver is clearly communicated and that what we build stays aligned with company strategic goals.

Right now my team is the one behind FORM's image recognition platform, which serves hundreds of the world's top brands. I built a lot of it as an engineer before I led it. I still shape its system design and architecture alongside our principal engineer and product partner, and keep a hand in the code through agentic engineering and the practices and tooling that let the rest of the team work that way.

Outside of work, I'm a family history archivist and maker.

positions.title: Lead Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Lead the team that owns FORM's image recognition platform, from public APIs (including IRaaS) to workflow orchestration and reporting
• Manage 6 direct reports through 1:1s, performance reviews, and career development
• Doubled the team from 3 through hiring and onboarding
• Partner with department- and executive-level product and engineering leadership on planning, priorities, and resourcing
• Stay hands-on through agentic engineering; built the team's Claude Code workspace of specialist agents, skills, and shared practices
• De-risk work with technical spikes before the team commits; coordinate across ML, mobile, web, and product
• Partner with customer success and other commercial teams to raise product literacy and support new customer use cases, and am usually the first to answer general questions in cross-team channels
• Oversaw the migration of image recognition orchestration to Temporal, halving processing latency
• Led the integration side of bringing Trax image recognition into FORM's pipeline post-merger: designed the internal API contracts that bridge the two systems and coordinated across business units to consolidate processing onto one architecture
positions.insights: People Development, AI Agents and +5 skills

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Served as technical lead for image recognition architecture and roadmap, serving hundreds of customers including major enterprise accounts
• Architected and led delivery of IRaaS, FORM's external image recognition API, built for 100x traffic bursts; partnered directly with Google Cloud engineering to validate scaling behavior and resource stewardship at volume
• Wrote the GCP region-migration playbook we used to move image recognition processing through multiple regional degradations, enabled by the configurable orchestration layer I designed
• Served as incident commander for most production incidents; unified GCP monitoring and PagerDuty alerting
• Aligned ML, web, mobile, and reporting teams on service contracts
• Championed company-wide Go standards; mentored, onboarded, and interviewed engineers
positions.insights: Incident Command, System Integration and +3 skills

positions.title: Backend Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Led the move from a homegrown orchestrator to Google Cloud Workflows, the foundation for the image recognition pipeline and IRaaS
• Designed, alongside our principal engineer, the system of record for image recognition configs, inputs, and model outputs
• Migrated PhotoWorks, our reporting app, from NoSQL to Postgres with zero data loss and zero downtime, not even a maintenance window
• Normalized the PhotoWorks domain model, making responses 5x faster for large enterprise customers
• Cut service downtime ~90% through architecture and stack upgrades
positions.insights: Go (Programming Language), Apache Kafka and +5 skills

positions.title: GCP Software Engineer
positions.description:
• Led Google Cloud support in Kion's cloud governance product, from architecture through customer escalations
• Built the microservices, internal SDKs, and docs the wider team used to extend GCP support
• Shipped full-stack features in Go and Angular
positions.insights: Go (Programming Language) and Google Cloud Platform (GCP)

organizations.description: I served as the Vice-President of Norsemen, the first-year men's choir at Luther College. I sang alongside some of the most talented musicians I have ever met, and I am proud to be a member of the brotherhood.
